$comment: Observability retention, sampling, queue bounds, and taxonomy. Not a UI knob. Missing required keys fail boot. Never put secrets here.
_memoryTelemetryComment: Readiness pass (2026-09-04): a durable (persisted, not in-memory-only) memory sample on a much coarser cadence than processTelemetryIntervalMs, specifically so a future silent death has real Argus-side memory-trend history to examine instead of relying on Windows' own external resource-exhaustion detector (the only evidence available for the Sept 2-3 deaths). Thresholds are evidence-labeled, not asserted precise: warning=2048MB sits above every healthy Node RSS baseline observed this session (600-800MB in the first 30-60min); critical=3584MB sits just under the ~3.85GB Node RSS peak that immediately preceded a prior silent death - close enough to alert before reaching that exact danger zone, not a proven safe ceiling. Recalibrate once a full RTH session's real Node memory curve (post Chronos-leak-fix) exists.
_memoryTelemetryCommittedComment: Readiness audit (2026-09-04) found the RSS thresholds above structurally CANNOT see the real Chronos failure mode on this Windows host. Measured live: the sidecar held 15,245.9MB of pagefile/commit charge and 6,451 OS threads while reporting 469.9MB working set - Windows had trimmed the working set, so this sampler had recorded level=NORMAL for hours against a process consuming ~30% of the host's ~50.9GB commit limit. Crucially, that instance had served ZERO inferences (/health lastInferenceMs was null), so commit growth of this shape is NOT explained by the torch.inference_mode() autograd-retention fix alone - thread accumulation in ThreadingHTTPServer is the larger contributor and remains open. These thresholds therefore watch COMMITTED memory (psutil memory_info().vms - pagefile charge on Windows, virtual size on POSIX) via the new numeric /health field committedMemoryMb. HONESTY: no committed-memory baseline for a FRESHLY started, healthy Chronos+FinBERT has been measured yet, so both numbers are provisional bounds chosen from the degraded measurement, not a calibrated healthy range - warning=6144MB and critical=12288MB both sit below the observed 15,245.9MB and leave real headroom under the commit limit. Expect the currently-running (degraded) sidecar to report CRITICAL immediately; that is the intended behaviour. Re-derive both once a fresh restart's real curve exists.
